Item Name: 1930s Bauhaus Chair by Mart Stam Dark Yellow (RAL 1021 Rapeseed Yellow)
Description: This Bauhaus chair by Mart Stam from the 1930s is lacquered in RAL 1021 Rapeseed Yellow, a rich, deep shade of yellow that gives the chrome-plated steel tube frame a colour effect unusually warm for Bauhaus furniture. The frame of bent chrome-plated steel tube works as a cantilever: with no rear legs, the tube itself provides the springing, which gives the seat a noticeable lightness. Seat and backrest are made of moulded beech plywood, clamped directly into the steel tube frame. Czechoslovak production of these chairs was closely tied to Thonet from the 1930s onwards and served the Europe-wide market for cantilever chairs after Stam and Breuer. The chrome frame is in very good condition, and the yellow lacquer is freshly applied. As a dining chair, this 1930s cantilever chair suits tables 75 to 78 cm in height. In a study or dining room it sets a clearly historical accent. Other colours are available on request from the existing stock of unrestored chairs.

Item Name: 1930s Bauhaus Chair by Mart Stam Pistachio Green (RAL 6019 White Green)
Description: This Bauhaus cantilever chair by Mart Stam from the 1930s has a factory fresh lacquer finish in RAL 6019 White Green, a cool pistachio green that forms a precise contrast with the chrome plated steel tube frame. Mart Stam developed the cantilever concept further in 1926: no rear leg, but a continuous bent steel tube whose elasticity provides the springing. Seat and backrest are made of moulded beech plywood, which gives the Bauhaus chair its clear seat geometry. The steel tube frame is chrome plated and in very good condition. Production took place in Czechoslovakia, where several manufacturers made the cantilever chairs for the European market from the early 1930s, in close association with Thonet. With a seat height of 45 cm and an overall height of 82 cm, this 1930s chair suits the dining room or the desk. Placed in a living room or study, it takes on a formal role as a Bauhaus chair without effort. Whoever prefers a different colour scheme can choose from the available stock of unrestored chairs and specify the colour individually.

Item Name: 1930s Bauhaus Chair by Mart Stam Pigeon Blue
Description: This Bauhaus cantilever chair by Mart Stam from the 1930s shows the design language that shaped Czechoslovak furniture production of that decade. The seat and backrest are made of moulded beech plywood, high-gloss lacquered in RAL 5014 Pigeon Blue. The chrome-plated steel tube frame traces the characteristic cantilever curve and creates a slightly springy seating position. The smooth lacquer surface reflects the light and gives the chair a cool, graphic presence. Mart Stam's design was produced in large numbers by various manufacturers in the 1930s. This example is finished in Pigeon Blue. Other colour variants are available on request. With a seat width of 39 cm, a depth of 50 cm and an overall height of 82 cm at a seat height of 45 cm, this Bauhaus chair suits the dining table, the study or as an accent chair in the living area. The piece comes from the Czech Republic and is in excellent condition.

The kitchen sideboard combines timeless design with practical functionality. Made from solid softwood (pine), this three-door sideboard stands for stability, craftsmanship, and clean lines. The white chalk paint gives the furniture a bright, friendly look, while the natural, waxed worktop provides a warm contrast. The combination of open glass display cabinets, numerous drawers, and generous storage space makes it the perfect solution for the kitchen, dining room, or living area.

Whether as a classic country-style kitchen sideboard, a solid wood dresser, or a stylish storage cabinet, this piece of furniture adapts to a wide variety of interior styles. The high-quality workmanship and natural grain of the pine wood underline the durable character of the piece. Each sideboard is manufactured in our own workshop with a focus on craftsmanship.

Most of the materials used come from original historical pieces that have been carefully restored and reused. New components are only added where necessary for functional or stability reasons. The result is a piece of furniture with a lived-in feel and contemporary everyday practicality.

This solid wood kitchen dining table in solid pine embodies the furniture tradition of the German country house: built to last, without superfluous gesture. The pine is stained and waxed, giving the surface a warm, matt finish and leaving the natural grain of the softwood visible. Beneath the tabletop sits an integrated drawer that keeps cutlery or kitchen utensils within reach at the table. At 110 cm wide and 80 cm deep, this kitchen dining table seats four people and fits into smaller kitchens as easily as into generous dining areas. The height of 78 cm lies within the ergonomic standard range for dining furniture. The turned legs follow the classic design language of rural furniture tradition and give the table its familiar, down-to-earth silhouette. In a farmhouse kitchen, a country style dining room or as a robust everyday table, the solid pine table combines with wooden chairs, benches or mixed vintage furnishings. Made in Germany according to traditional craftsmanship, this piece stands for a furniture tradition that brings function and material directly together.

This bedside table set consists of two well-proportioned companions in solid spruce. The surfaces are finished in white, through which the natural grain shows subtly and gives the piece a restrained, elegant expression. The tops were left natural and waxed, creating a warm contrast. Handles in solid brass set discreet accents and complete the classic appearance.

At a compact 40 x 35 x 70 cm, the bedside tables suit bedrooms in a country house style as well as naturally toned modern interiors. As part of our range of solid softwood furniture, these pieces are also newly crafted in our own workshop with artisanal care. A durable, solid wood solution for those who value natural materials and classic design.

Much of the material used comes from historic original components, carefully restored and reused. New parts are added only where functional or structural reasons require it. The result is a piece of furniture with lived-in substance and contemporary everyday usability.
Bedside table in solid spruce with a drawer, finished in natural wax, with handles in solid brass. Softwood WH126 model, German made, in very good condition.

Item Name: Softwood Half Sideboard WH65 in White
Description: Half sideboard out of solid spruce, with a natural, waxed top and two internal shelves

This display cabinet is a sleek, upright storage unit made of solid pine and part of our series of high-quality softwood furniture. Crafted from solid pine and painted white, it brings a bright, calming ambiance to living rooms, dining rooms, or hallways. The natural grain of the softwood remains visible despite the white finish, lending the piece its handcrafted character.

The upper section of the softwood display cabinet features a glass-fronted storage compartment with adjustable shelves, ideal for displaying dishes, books, or decorative objects. The lower, closed section complements its function as a solid wood cabinet and provides additional storage space. Thanks to its narrow footprint, this pine display cabinet is also suitable for smaller rooms without sacrificing presence.

As a softwood piece, it combines classic proportions with practical everyday use. Each piece is handcrafted in our own workshop, representing durable workmanship, natural materials, and timeless design. This solid pine display cabinet complements both country-style interiors and minimalist design concepts, blending harmoniously into existing spaces.

A large portion of the materials used comes from original historical parts that have been carefully restored and reused. New components are only added where necessary for functional or stability reasons. The result is a piece of furniture with a lived-in feel and contemporary everyday usability.

The display cabinet combines classic elegance with practical functionality. Made from solid pine and painted white, it impresses with its light, timeless character. In the upper section, the display cabinet offers two shelves behind glass-framed doors – ideal for stylishly presenting crockery, books, or decorations. Three generous drawers in the lower section provide additional storage space. The high-quality construction from solid softwood and the finely crafted details make this piece a highlight in any room. As part of our softwood furniture series, the display cabinet is manufactured in our own factory with a focus on craftsmanship. Ideal for anyone looking for durable, authentic country house furniture made from solid wood.

Most of the materials used come from original historical pieces that have been carefully restored and reused. New components are only added where necessary for functional or stability reasons. The result is a piece of furniture with a lived-in character and contemporary everyday practicality.

Item Name: Kitchen Cabinet in Softwood and Pine
Description:
The kitchen cabinet combines classic country house style with compact design. Made from solid softwood (pine), this white-painted cabinet with clean lines and charming details such as round feet and elegant fittings brings a bright, timeless aesthetic to any kitchen. The lower unit offers generous storage space with a door and drawer, while the upper section with a glass door, two small drawers, and open shelving creates additional space for supplies, dishes, or decorations. The surface is finished in a subtle white that fits perfectly with both modern and traditional interior styles. Like all furniture in the Weichholz series, this model is also newly manufactured – with craftsmanship and natural materials.

Most of the materials used come from original historical parts that have been carefully restored and reused. New components are only added where necessary for functional or stability reasons. The result is a piece of furniture with lived-in substance and contemporary everyday practicality.

The bookcase is made from solid, waxed spruce and belongs to our series of high-quality softwood furniture. With its simple design language and warm wooden surface, it combines a timeless look with functional design. The shelves are individually height-adjustable by means of classic ratchet strips and offer flexible storage space for books, decorative objects or everyday items.

As part of a country-house interior or combined with modern elements, the shelf convinces with its material quality, craftsmanship and proportions. The solid spruce construction shows off the natural grain particularly well. Each piece is newly made in our own workshop with a craftsman's attention to detail, a durable, authentic piece of furniture with character. Ideal for anyone who loves real wood and solid furniture, also in Berlin and the surrounding area.
Bedside cabinet in solid spruce with a drawer, naturally waxed, with handles in solid brass.

This Art Deco wall coat rack from the 1930s unites French design sensibility with the polished aluminium tube that was typical of the period's material language. The slender construction shows the characteristic elegance of Art Deco through curved lines and a clear vertical articulation, which gives the piece a light impression despite its 180 cm height. The polished aluminium reflects light and creates a discreet sheen that blends harmoniously into refined interiors. With only 20 cm of depth this aluminium tube coat rack takes up barely any space and suits hallways or entrance areas where room is at a premium. The 88 cm width offers plenty of hanging surface for coats and accessories without dominating the wall. As a French Art Deco coat rack it carries the imprint of an era in which functional design and aesthetic ambition formed a natural unity. The excellent condition of preservation underscores the quality of the original workmanship and makes this piece an authentic addition for lovers of this style.

Item Name: Armchair 'Fjord' by Patricia Urquiola for Moroso, 2005, Set of 2
Description: The Fjord armchair by Patricia Urquiola for Moroso is one of the best known designs of the early 21st century from the Italian furniture maker. The model was designed in 2002, the two examples offered here were made in 2005. Both are upholstered in white leather in the 'Pelle bianco puro' finish with decorative topstitching that follows the contour of the shell. The seat shell is made of cold-formed polyurethane foam and carries the organic form of the armchair. The base and shaft in powder-coated steel are square and set a formal contrast to the soft shell. Fully swivelling and fitted with a high back, the Moroso swivel armchair is suited to long periods of sitting. At 100 × 70 × 103 cm it is conceived on a generous scale. In a living room or a representative reception area, the white Fjord armchair sets a clear focal point. As a pair, both chairs can be arranged as a conversation group or as a symmetrical counterpart to a lounge table. 'MOROSO' manufacturer labels are present on the underside. Minor scratches on the base are documented, the overall condition is very good.

Item Name: 1930s Bauhaus Side Table, Chrome-Plated Steel Tube
Description:
This 1930s Bauhaus side table comes from Czechoslovak production and follows the design language that Czech licensed makers such as Halabala and Slezak shaped in that decade. The frame is made of chrome-plated steel tube, bent into splayed, outward-curving legs on black rubber glides. Two round wooden shelves are stained black and show clearly visible ash grain.

The upper top is larger than the lower shelf, which gives the piece its characteristic proportions. Chrome-plated steel tube and dark stained wood create a contrast of materials that belongs to the Bauhaus aesthetic of the early 1930s. Black rubber glides protect the floor.

As a 1930s side table, the piece has two tiers and is as useful as a surface beside the sofa as it is as an occasional piece in a study. With a diameter of approx. 70 cm it has a presence in surface area without taking up much space. In a Berlin period apartment, the chrome steel tube side table pairs with other Bauhaus furniture of the era as well as with contemporary mixed interiors. No manufacturer attribution available.

Item Name: 1950s Mid-Century Arne Jacobsen Armchair in Teak, by Fritz Hansen
Description:
This Arne Jacobsen armchair from the Series 7 by Fritz Hansen, model 3207, was designed in 1955 and is available here. The seat shell is made of laminated, steam-pressed teak veneer, which Jacobsen shaped into a flowing, one-piece form. Armrests and shell come from the same material and merge without a visible transition.

The four-legged steel frame is slim in proportion and fitted with black plastic glides. At a width of 61 cm the chair seats the body well without additional upholstery, as the shell shape follows the natural curve of the body.

As a Mid-Century armchair, the 3207 suits the dining table just as well as an occasional chair in a study or living room. In a Berlin period apartment it combines with dark post-war wooden tables as readily as with modern surfaces in oak or marble. Finding three chairs of the same model and age as a matching set is rare. Signs of wear consistent with age are present on the armrests.

Item Name: 1930s Bauhaus Sofa with Steel Tube and Leather Upholstery
Description:
This 1930s Bauhaus sofa with a chrome-plated steel tube frame and cream leather upholstery shows the design logic of Classic Modernism in precise form. Rounded side cheeks of chrome-plated steel tube enclose the upholstery on both sides. The seat sits low at 40 cm, and the overall height is 66 cm. Two loose cushions in cream serve as back support: a cylindrical neck roll and a flat square cushion, which can be positioned as needed.

At 190 cm wide and 80 cm deep, this Bauhaus sofa works as well as a récamière or day bed as it does as a classic piece of seating. The cream leather has a smooth, carefully maintained surface and is in very good condition. In a living room with period character or in spaces with clean lines, the piece acts as a calm, consistently designed centrepiece.

Made in Germany in the 1930s, this vintage Bauhaus sofa belongs to the generation of design classics that established the interplay of steel tube and upholstery as a language of form in its own right.

This Art Deco floor lamp by Mazda from the 1930s follows the torchère principle: the light is thrown upwards onto the ceiling, creating even, indirect ambient light. The black lacquered wooden shaft tapers slightly towards the top, structured by chrome-plated metal rings and slender transition pieces. At the top sits a wide, flared opal glass shade that diffuses the light softly. At the base, a circular chrome-plated metal foot keeps the slender construction in balance.

At 190 cm in height and with a shade diameter of 36 cm, this 1930s floor lamp has enough presence for high rooms without being intrusive. Living rooms, libraries or bedrooms with suitable ceiling height benefit from the calm lighting atmosphere that an opal glass floor lamp of this kind creates.

Mazda was one of the leading manufacturers of home lighting in France during the interwar period. The piece comes from France and is in excellent condition.

Item Name: 1950s Mid-Century Bar in Art Deco Style
Description:
This 1950s Art Deco bar shows what a thorough restoration can make of a discarded piece of furniture. The semicircular front in rich burgundy is divided into three horizontal panels, separated by trim strips of polished aluminium and stainless steel. In place of the original faux leather covering, the front now carries acrylic glass with precisely placed metal strips, giving the surface a clear, robust quality. Newly lacquered Resopal forms the work surface.

At 212 cm wide and 144 cm high, this 1950s home bar is designed to stand freely. A wine rack and a wine cooler have been integrated inside, so the piece is fully usable as a functional bar. The chrome-plated railing along the top edge, carried by slender metal supports, is characteristic of bar architecture of that decade.

As an Art Deco bar in excellent condition, it suits spacious living rooms, loft apartments or commercial spaces. The character of the German original has been preserved, and the fittings have been fully renewed for contemporary use.

This Bauhaus wardrobe from the 1930s was made by Slezak in Czechoslovakia, one of the manufacturers that brought the tubular steel furniture of those years into series production. The body is made of lacquered blockboard, its surface closed and without visible wood grain, while the frame of chrome-plated steel tube carries the wardrobe and lifts it off the floor. This construction was the real break with the furniture making of the 19th century, because the wardrobe no longer stands on feet but in a frame. With a width of 120 cm, a depth of 59 cm and a height of 190 cm, the wardrobe holds a complete wardrobe of clothes, and the depth is sufficient for hangers placed crosswise. In the bedroom of an old-building flat, a 1930s wardrobe of this height finds the right proportion to the room heights. The piece is restored and in excellent condition, the lacquered surfaces are even, and the chrome on the frame is bright and complete.

This 1930s Bauhaus cabinet is lacquered black and stands on a steel tube base, which gives it a clear, uncluttered appearance despite its height of 189 cm. The body is made of lacquered wood, the finish is closed and silky, without grain or structure, so the piece stands in the room as a calm black surface. The steel tube frames the lower edge and lifts the cabinet off the floor, which takes away the impression of heaviness. With a width of 130 cm and a depth of 55 cm, the cabinet offers storage for a complete wardrobe or for files and books in a study. Anyone living in an old building with high ceilings will find the right proportion in a 1930s cabinet of this size, as lower pieces look lost there. The piece has been restored and is in excellent condition, the black lacquer is even and free of chips, and the steel tube at the base is free of rust.

Item Name: 1930s Bauhaus Desk, Ebonised with Linoleum Top
Description: This Bauhaus desk from the 1930s is ebonised and carries a black linoleum work surface, a combination that was common in German office furniture of those years. The wooden carcass was stained black throughout and then hand polished with shellac, creating a deep, silky sheen in which light breaks softly. The drawers and the top are edged in solid beech, whose light edge visibly frames the black. Handles and frame are made of chrome-plated steel tube and take up the formal language of the Bauhaus. Linoleum is the right surface for writing, as it is neither cold nor slippery and absorbs pressure. At 120 cm wide and 65 cm deep, the 1930s desk also fits into a smaller study, and the working height of 76 cm meets today's standards. The piece has been fully restored and is in excellent condition.

This 1950s bar cart by Torck comes from Belgian production and shows the clear tubular construction the manufacturer became known for. The frame is made of chrome-plated steel tube, running in one continuous curve from the castors to the push handle and carrying both trays. The shelves are framed in black lacquer and fitted with dark red smoked glass, which catches the light and gives the cart depth. On the lower level sits a chrome-plated bottle holder that securely holds three bottles while the bar cart is being moved. Four castors roll easily, so glasses and drinks can be wheeled from the dining room to the living room without rearranging. At 77 cm wide and 73 cm high, this Mid-Century bar cart stands at table height and also serves as a side surface next to the sofa between evenings. The condition is excellent, the chrome, lacquer and glass panels are complete and free of damage.

Item Name: Original Knoll Saarinen Tulip Coffee Table
Description: This Tulip coffee table is an original by Knoll International, designed by Eero Saarinen, and shows the all-white finish for which the series became known. The base is made of cast aluminium and sweeps out of a slender column into a wide, flat-flaring plate that carries the table with no visible joint. The round top has a diameter of 91 cm and is plastic-coated on an MDF carrier board, which keeps the surface resistant to moisture and wear. Saarinen set out to eliminate the clutter of table legs beneath furniture, and that is exactly what the Tulip table achieves in the living room: the floor stays clear around it, and armchairs can be drawn up as desired. At 39 cm high, it suits usual sofa seat heights. The condition is excellent, the lacquer and coating are free of chips, so this Mid-Century design classic is ready for immediate use.

This cantilever office chair by Drabert combines the springy tubular steel frame of classic modernism with black leather upholstery. The frame is made of chrome-plated steel tube bent in a single piece and carries the seat and backrest without rear legs, so the chair gives slightly under load. Seat cushion and back pad are generously filled and covered in leather that has softened over decades of use and taken on an even, dark patina. The armrests are made of black stained wood, hand-polished with shellac, and feel pleasantly warm to the touch. With a width of 56 cm, a depth of 60 cm and a seat height of 46 cm, the office chair is designed for daily desk work, but works equally well as a side chair in the living room or as a seat at the dining table. Drabert built seating for offices and administration in Minden for decades, and the workmanship of this chair shows why these pieces are sought after.

Item Name: 1950s RB3 Cantilever Chairs by Mauser, Set of 4
Description: This set of four RB3 cantilever chairs from the 1950s comes from the Alfons Mauser Werke in Waldeck and goes back to the design by Mart Stam, who presented the first chair without back legs in 1926. The frame is made of chrome-plated steel tube, bent in one continuous run, letting the chair spring on two runners. Seat and backrest are moulded plywood, stained black and polished with shellac, so the surface shines deeply and the wood structure remains visible beneath the black. Finding four identical Bauhaus cantilever chairs as a set is rare, as these chairs were sold individually for decades. At the dining table the springing frame yields with every movement, which makes longer sitting more comfortable than on a rigid four-legged chair. The seat height of 43 cm suits tables between 70 and 76 cm. Chrome and polish are evenly preserved on all four chairs and show signs of use without being damaged.

This Art Deco side cabinet of French manufacture combines a tall, very narrow carcass with a walnut veneer front laid in a mirrored cut, which produces a symmetrical grain pattern. Sides stained black and hand polished with shellac frame this warm wooden surface and give it depth. Chrome-plated steel tube edges the front and joins at the bottom in a continuous loop on which the carcass stands. The door is hinged on the left, which makes this cabinet the counterpart of the right-hinged model and allows it to be placed as a pair. At 109.5 cm high, 47 cm wide and 25.5 cm deep, the side cabinet also fits in a hallway or a wall niche, where it holds glasses, books or papers. Restored and in excellent condition, with a closed polish and complete chrome, the piece suits living room, dining room and study alike.

This French Art Deco side cabinet has a walnut veneer front whose mirrored grain builds across the entire door and meets in the middle to form a symmetrical pattern. The sides and top are stained black and hand-polished with shellac, creating a deep, slightly reflective surface that can only be achieved with this technique. The chrome-plated steel tube frame runs vertically up the front edges and closes at the bottom in a runner that lifts the carcase off the floor. The door is hinged on the right. At 47 cm wide and only 25.5 cm deep, with a height of 109.5 cm, the side cabinet fits into a niche, beside a door or in the hallway, where it provides storage without narrowing the passage. Behind the door are shelves for glasses, books or office supplies. The piece is restored and in excellent condition, veneer and shellac polish are intact throughout.

This 1950s steel tube chair comes from Italian production and carries the Bauhaus idea of the bent tube into a round, almost sculptural form. The frame is cold-bent from chrome-plated steel tube and forms a semicircle in plan, serving as backrest, armrests and base ring at once. The seat is round and upholstered in black fabric, and the back roll carries the same upholstery, sitting exactly at lumbar height. Seat height 46 cm, overall height 78 cm, width 54 cm: the chair is compact enough for a dining table and comfortable enough to sit in for longer. At a desk, at a round kitchen table or on its own as a seat in the bedroom, this Mid Century chair works equally well. The chrome is preserved all round and shows only the fine loss of shine that five decades leave behind. The fabric cover is as good as new, so the chair can be put to use straight away.

This 1930s Bauhaus dining table was made by Slezak in Czechoslovakia after a design by Marcel Breuer and shows the principle that defined furniture production of those years: a heavy top on an extremely light base. The square top measures 80 by 80 cm, is veneered and lacquered deep black, so the surface looks matt and closed. The frame is made of chrome-plated steel tube, whose four hoops join at the bottom to form a cross and carry the table without aprons. This leaves legroom on all four sides, and the dining table comfortably seats four people although it takes up only one square metre of floor space. For small kitchens and period apartment rooms, that is exactly the advantage over a table with an apron. The height of 70 cm matches the usual seat height. The chrome shows the even patina of ninety years, and the lacquered surface is well preserved.

Item Name: Art Deco Mazda Table Lamp, Black
Description: This Art Deco table lamp by Mazda from the 1930s features the typical chalice-shaped shade in white opal glass on a black lacquered, tapering stem. The socket and base plate are made of copper, polished to a red-gold finish, which sets a warm contrast against the deep black of the stem. The opal glass scatters the light upwards towards the ceiling, so the room is lit indirectly and softly, with no glare source in the field of view. A pull switch with a brass chain operates the lamp directly at the head. At 77 cm high, this 1930s table lamp is large enough to serve as a light source for the whole living space on a sideboard or chest of drawers. Beside an armchair it becomes a reading corner. The French Mazda lamps of this type are regarded as Art Deco classics and have become rare in this size and with undamaged opal glass.

This Kaiser Idell desk lamp 6632 Präsident is one of the best known Bauhaus lamps and carries the characteristic dome shaped shade with the mounted articulated head. The shade is lacquered a deep black with a high gloss, and the light is gathered within it and thrown downwards without glare. Arm and base are made of chrome-plated steel, and the grip on the arm is finished in black, so the lamp can be adjusted even while switched on. The ball joint at the base allows the cone of light to be swivelled across the full width of the desk. At 48 cm high with a shade diameter of 30 cm, the desk lamp is designed for a workplace where people read and write, not for decorative mood lighting. It sits as rightly on a secretary desk in an old building as on a modern desk. Christian Dell shaped the design language of this series, and the Präsident variant is the largest and calmest of them.

This small side table from the 1930s carries a round top of black glass in a nickel-plated metal frame. The base is designed as a curved swan neck rising from a bell-shaped foot and holding the top offset to one side. The metal shows the warm, slightly matt sheen of nickel plating as was usual in the 1930s, with fine traces of use that do not disfigure the frame. The black glass top measures 30 cm in diameter, and the height of 50 cm matches the armrest of an armchair. The side table therefore stands exactly where a cup, a book or a glass needs to be put down, without a large piece of furniture getting in the way. In an old-building flat next to a leather armchair the table looks just as fitting as in a pared-back modern living room. The offset base allows the top to be slid over the edge of the armchair, which a straight column table cannot do.

This Bauhaus oak shelf from the 1930s combines two sturdy oak boards with a frame of chromed steel tube. The shelves show a distinctly grained, dark stained surface whose pores remain visible and give the wood a matt, warm depth. The steel tube is bent in wide radii and carries both levels without added screws, which gives the piece a light appearance despite its mass. With a width of 87 cm and a depth of only 36 cm, the shelf fits in the hallway, where it holds keys, post and bags, just as well as behind the sofa as a console. The height of 77 cm matches the working height of a table, so the upper board can also be used while standing. Anyone looking for a 1930s shelf with real substance gets a German Bauhaus piece whose chrome shines evenly with age and whose oak has darkened over the decades.

Item Name: 1990s B20 Cantilever Chair by Tecta, Set of 4
Description: The 1990 B 20 cantilever chair by Tecta is a timeless piece that embodies the charm of Mid-Century design. Made in Germany, this chair combines high-quality steel tube with an elegant plastic weave that gives it not only stability but also an appealing aesthetic. With dimensions of 50 cm in width and 59 cm in depth, it offers a comfortable seat height of 47 cm. The chair is in excellent condition and brings a touch of design classic into any room. Ideal for modern living and working spaces, it sets stylish accents. The combination of functionality and design makes this chair a valuable addition to your home. With 6 pieces available, now is the perfect time to acquire this unique chair and give your space more character.

This Bauhaus cabinet from the 1930s comes from German production and gathers the core idea of the classical modern movement into an upright, slender piece of furniture. The carcass is made from veneered chipboard and finished with a silk matte lacquer, while the upper compartment with its sliding glass doors appears in a strong purple red and gives the cabinet a clear note of colour. Chrome-plated steel tube forms the frame and the handles, letting the Bauhaus cabinet read light and precise. Four closed compartments and two open shelves create storage for books, files and collectibles; the sliding glass doors keep the contents visible and the front closed at the same time. At 140 cm wide, 45 cm deep and 166 cm high, the piece fits as naturally into an old town apartment as into a modern interior and, in its excellent condition, remains a dependable piece for a library, a home office or a guest room.

Item Name: 1930s Bauhaus Console Table B12 by Marcel Breuer, White
Description: This Bauhaus console table by Marcel Breuer dates from the 1930s and shows the reduced design language that shaped the work of the Hungarian designer around the Bauhaus. Two panels of white, lacquered wood-based board rest on a chrome-plated steel tube frame, a calm contrast between bright white and cool metal. The construction is slim and lightly drawn, the chrome-plated steel tube steps back behind the pale surfaces and lets the console seem almost floating despite its height. At 70 cm wide and 71 cm tall it occupies a wall, a hallway or the space beside a sofa without pressing. Two flat, uncluttered panels offer room for pictures, vases and a lamp, making the piece as usable as it is pleasant to look at. As an original of the classic modern era from German manufacture the console table fits an Altbau apartment as well as a modern interior. In excellent condition, with white lacquer and smooth chrome, it brings an ordered Bauhaus design into any room.

Item Name: Anglepoise Table Lamp Herbert Terry & Sons
Description: This Bauhaus table lamp by Anglepoise comes from England and was developed by George Carwardine for Herbert Terry & Sons. The frame is made of chrome-plated steel, the shade of polished aluminium, whose surface reflects the light strongly. The articulated double arm with its coil springs and constant spring mechanism can be set in any position and stays there. The stepped metal base ensures a secure stance, even though the lamp reaches out widely at a height of 130 cm. As a desk lamp in a study, it lights up a book, keyboard or sketchpad exactly where the work is done. In period apartments this vintage Anglepoise lamp looks as fitting as in modern interiors. The black fabric cable complements the technical look. The English original is in excellent condition.

This Louis Seize wall mirror from France has an oval gilded wooden frame with handcarved ornaments of flowers, leaves and ribbon work that grow out from the sides of the frame. The gilding sits warm and full on the wood and shows the material depth that distinguishes original pieces of this period from reproductions. The inner edge of the oval is bordered by a bead and star frieze, a fine formal detail that structures the transition between frame and glass.
